extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament, parliamentary staff, and the general public (citizens and organised groups)
extracted.subtask_description: A factsheet guiding how the public should be engaged in parliamentary/legislative processes in Kenya — explains rights, duties, tools, organising steps, and exceptional limits. Focused on facilitating meaningful citizen input into lawmaking, oversight and financial/business of the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation is the involvement of those affected by a decision in the decision-making process; it encompasses a range of involvement from informing people about what Parliament is doing to delegating decisions to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is a process of interaction between an organisation and the public aimed at making acceptable and better decisions. The process involves informing and listening, dialogue, debate and analysis, and implementation of agreed solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should participate (inclusivity / non-discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in legislative processes is open to all members of the public, either individually or as organised groups; Parliament shall not bar anyone from participating on grounds such as age, race, colour, gender or political affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Constitution guarantees that no one shall be barred; participation may be individual or through organised groups. Equality in participation is underscored by Article 27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional duty of Parliament to facilitate participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament is mandated by Article 118(1)(b) to facilitate public participation and involvement in legislative and other business of the Assembly and its committees, and to conduct its business in an open manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a Bill is introduced and referred to a committee, the committee places adverts in the media requesting public views. Committees must take public views into consideration when preparing reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public have the right to petition Parliament on any matter within its authority, as provided under Article 119 and the Petitions to Parliament (Procedure) Act, No. 22 of 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions may request Parliament to consider enacting, amending or repealing legislation, or request removal of public officers under Article 251; petitions are a formal tool for raising matters for parliamentary consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to access information and freedom of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The freedom of expression (Article 33) and the right to access information (Article 35 and the Access to Information Act, No. 31 of 2016) guarantee citizens' ability to seek, receive and impart information during public participation processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliament proceedings are open and may be live-streamed (e.g., YouTube) to enhance transparency and enable informed participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality in participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 27 guarantees equal participation in decision-making processes including the legislative activities of Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality principle reinforces non-discrimination and equal access to participation mechanisms for all citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign power and duty to exercise it
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereign power belongs to the people and can be exercised directly through citizen participation or indirectly through elected leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle underscores that election of representatives does not negate the need for continuous citizen involvement in governance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in law-making (procedural expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: During law-making, committees must solicit and consider public views when a Bill is referred to them and make sittings/committee business open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees advertise for public views; the public may submit written memoranda; public hearings and committee reports should reflect consideration of public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in financial matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation must be integrated into consideration of financial matters per Articles 201, 221 and 232 of the Constitution and the Public Finance Management Act, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public can make submissions or attend public hearings to give views on budget estimates and other financial matters; standing orders and PFM Act elaborate procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The public can participate in parliamentary oversight activities (holding the Executive to account, approving appointments, removal from office, reviewing statutory instruments) by expressing views and petitioning Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public can provide grounds for removal of officers, submit opinions on suitability of appointees, and engage in consultations related to oversight inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools for participation: Petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions are a formal tool for public participation provided for under Article 119; the public can petition on matters within Parliament's authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions can address legislation, amendments, repeal, and removal of public officers; the Petition to Parliament (Procedure) Act governs process and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools for participation: Submissions / memoranda
rubrics_metrics.description: When Parliament or committees are considering Bills, statutory instruments, budget estimates or conducting inquiries, the public may make written submissions or memoranda on the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are solicited during bill consideration, approval hearings, or removal processes; memoranda may be presented regarding suitability of public officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools for participation: Public forums and hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Public forums provide face-to-face engagement between MPs and citizens for instant feedback; committees may undertake public hearings, meetings in and outside Parliament, and inspection visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public are free to attend committee meetings; field visits and in-person forums enable direct observation and interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organising public participation: Awareness and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating awareness is the first step in organising participation — placing adverts in mainstream print and electronic media to generate interest and increase citizen participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awareness-raising should target broad publics and affected groups to ensure turnout and informed contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organising public participation: Stakeholder identification (Involvement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify key stakeholders or interested groups, including those directly affected and those that can offer solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping affected groups and potential contributors improves relevance and quality of input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organising public participation: Contacting and inviting participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate to stakeholders in writing, invite them to meetings, and request submission of documents or memoranda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely written invitations and clear requests for submissions help witnesses prepare and participate effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organising public participation: Meetings and field visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold meetings to collect views and undertake field visits/inspection visits of projects as part of engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings should be planned to allow meaningful exchanges; field visits provide direct observation of project states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organising public participation: Feedback mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide feedback through drafting and tabling the resultant report so stakeholders see how their input was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closing the loop increases accountability and credibility of the participation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting public participation sessions (session management)
rubrics_metrics.description: During sessions, the action plan must be carried out for accountability; stakeholders should be provided necessary information, witnesses invited in time and allowed sufficient time to prepare oral or written submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective provision of information and reasonable preparation time enhance credibility and quality of contributions; follow the action plan to document proceedings and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of public and media (in-camera sessions) — exceptional circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional circumstances, in-camera sessions can be held under Article 118(2); the Speaker must be satisfied there are sufficient grounds to exclude the public and the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for in-camera sessions should state reasons for exclusion; exclusion is the exception and must be justified and approved by the Speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: International and regional obligations supporting participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Kenya's international/regional commitments (e.g., Rio Declaration Principle 10, Agenda 21, Manila Declaration, African Charter for Popular Participation) promote transparency, participation and access to information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commitments spur domestic steps to improve participation and are part of the normative justification for public participation practices.
